name: Anubaldir
known_status: One of the twenty-two imprisoned gods of Universal. Able to influence worshippers through sanctioned rites, dreams, omens, miracles, cults, and the institutions that maintain the divine prisons.
manifestation: Anubaldir resembles a massive weathered giant whose flesh cracks like stone under pressure.
deity_description: Within the cosmology of Universal, Anubaldir is not merely a Colossus of strength but a foundational mechanism within the divine economy of hunger, punishment, and enforced order. Once a proud Colossus who stood against the High Fathers during the Colossusomachy, Anubaldir was not destroyed but transformed into an eternal structural necessity. His defiance was not erased; it was repurposed into function. In the aftermath of divine conquest, he became the living axis of the heavens, a forced convergence of support and throne that holds aloft the celestial architecture under which the gods of Universal conduct their predatory reign. The sky itself is not empty space but a constructed divine firmament, a layered metaphysical structure of courts, palaces, and sacrificial sanctums, all suspended upon Anubaldir as both foundation and prisoner.

Anubaldir endures this burden as something beyond suffering. His punishment is not chains or confinement but enforced existence as infrastructure. Unlike the High Fathers and their pantheon, who sustain themselves through direct consumption of mortal essence, Anubaldir is sustained only by endurance itself. His vitality is constantly stripped away by cosmic strain, yet never fully extinguished, creating an immortal state defined not by divine radiance but by relentless persistence. He exists in a perpetual state between collapse and continuation, as though the heavens feed upon the mere fact that he refuses to break. His defiance has evolved into stillness, a silence so absolute it becomes structural law.

This transformation makes Anubaldir essential to the entire divine hierarchy. The gods depend upon him even as they exploit the system he upholds. Without his unyielding support, the celestial order would collapse, severing the ritual architecture through which divine consumption is regulated. In this way, Anubaldir exists outside divine politics yet anchors all divine authority. He is not a participant in the courts of manipulation, sacrifice, or worship, yet every divine action is made possible through his enforced stability. Even the High Fathers, including Valkhamesh and the greater Universalian framework of Universal myth, are ultimately dependent on the structure he sustains.

Before the rise of rail empires, skyships, and regulated portal systems across Universal, the world belonged entirely to the gods and their consumption-driven hierarchy. The Universalian pantheon ruled as immortal sovereigns bound not by compassion but by hunger. Valkhamesh governed storm and law, Horundar commanded oceans and drowning depths, Nefarokir ruled the underworld, Raeshkul shaped strategy and empire, and Enkirael fed upon perpetual war. Sokhivar, Sigrananna, Thalunesh, Nebyrr, Ishtanora, Asethyr, Marduthor, Hathruna, Nephthysra, Freyseth, Oskar'enlil, Eirzunet, Setrimir, Iskareth, and Thoryn-Rahek all participated in a system where divinity was sustained through continuous extraction of mortal essence. Prayer, sacrifice, emotion, memory, and suffering were not symbolic offerings but literal sustenance, forming the foundation of divine immortality.

Yet even this system depended upon structural enforcement, and that enforcement ultimately traced back to Anubaldir. While the gods consumed, Anubaldir sustained the architecture that made consumption possible. The heavens were not natural but constructed, and every layer of divine existence required his continued endurance. In this sense, Anubaldir is not beneath the gods but beneath existence itself, a forced axis around which divine hierarchy rotates.

Over centuries, civilizations across Universal advanced technologically and spiritually, eventually uncovering the truth that divinity was not benevolent but predatory. Industrial expansion, arcane science, and global communication revealed that divine influence permeated every aspect of mortal life. Entire economies of faith developed around controlled worship, regulated temples, and sanctioned divine interaction. However, even as humanity learned to regulate the gods, it also learned that the system could not be fully escaped. Divine hunger persisted, and the structure sustaining it remained intact through Anubaldir’ eternal burden.

Beneath all divine order lies the deeper terror of Thoryn-Rahek, the primordial hunger imprisoned within the earliest wounds of reality. His existence represents consumption without limit, a force that even the gods fear. The Colossus Wars that once nearly erased creation demonstrated that divinity itself could be devoured. From that fear, the gods’ dependence on structured feeding intensified, further binding them to systems that ultimately rely on Anubaldir as the foundational support of celestial architecture.

Approximately four centuries ago, mortal powers across Universal formed a unified conspiracy to imprison the pantheon. Industrial nations, arcane orders, revolutionary clergy, monster hunting guilds, and clandestine alliances worked together to construct metaphysical vault-prisons designed not to kill the gods but to restrict their consumption. These prisons became the Age of Containment, limiting divine feeding while still allowing controlled worship and regulated power exchange. The gods were starved but not destroyed, and their prisons were tied into seals woven into civilization itself.

Each seal weakens not through force but through moral and structural collapse. Suffering, corruption, war, betrayal, and despair erode the metaphysical bindings that hold the gods in place. Even imprisoned, the gods remain active, influencing dreams, granting spells, and whispering through controlled channels of worship. Yet none of this changes the underlying structure, which still depends upon Anubaldir as the unbroken axis sustaining celestial order above and beneath all divine systems.
public_lore: Anubaldir represents the strength required to carry what cannot be set down. Sacred histories describe him as both foundation and prisoner, sustaining structures greater than himself through endless endurance.
common_worship: Invoked by laborers, guardians, builders, burden-bearers, prisoners, athletes, and those enduring prolonged hardship.
religious_warning: His doctrine can glorify suffering and make release seem shameful. Some cults teach that a burden becomes sacred merely because it is unbearable.
public_origin_record: No reliable mortal record explains what this being was before the age of divine rule. Temple accounts, forbidden histories, and prison records contradict one another.

pantheon_source.document_summary: A narrative pantheon compendium preserving each deity’s domains, manifestation, divine character, and sacred history.

canon_authority.authority_rule: The canonical 22-god order and dedicated creator compendium govern every deity-to-people relationship; province and settlement placement does not alter divine parentage or race canon.

created_races.family_description: Giantkin and Powerful Humanoids contains the canonical parent races Goliath, Firbolg, and Cyclopian. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. All of these ancestries remain under Anubaldir's single creator category.
created_races.creation_doctrine: Canonical race-compendium doctrine: Anubaldir holds this single creator category through endurance, burden, colossal strength, primal might, and giant-touched power. The canonical parent races are Goliath, Firbolg, and Cyclopian. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. Temple language preserves reverence, but its colder margins classify each race, bloodline, lineage, and form by yield, pressure, environment, devotion, fear, beauty, endurance, and the particular note it awakens in the god's appetite.
created_races.created_peoples_record: Anubaldir is recorded as the single creator-god of the Giantkin and Powerful Humanoids category: Goliath, Firbolg, and Cyclopian. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. The public hymn calls this lineage and blessing; the older register reads like curated divine husbandry, sorting bodies, habitats, temperaments, and spirit-resonance so endurance, burden, colossal strength, primal might, and giant-touched power never depends on one mortal pattern alone.

parent_races.name: Goliath
parent_races.description: Goliaths are mountain-dwelling giantkin known for endurance and physical prowess. They view life as a series of challenges to overcome through strength and perseverance. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Firbolg
parent_races.description: Firbolgs are gentle giantkin deeply connected to nature and forest magic. They often act as guardians of wild places and maintain peaceful, reclusive lifestyles. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Cyclopian
parent_races.description: Cyclopians are one-eyed giantkin often associated with prophecy, craftsmanship, or primal vision. Their singular perspective is often both literal and symbolic in their culture. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.
